approach: One definition decides where records are read from. records_worktree_path lives in athena-data paths.rs beside repo_state_dir. A helper in athena-core store.rs returns the tip of refs/heads/athena/records when that tip has entries under records/. Otherwise it returns the working-tree fallback. Tree readers get Records::load_current and RecordSet::load_current. These swap the caller's treeish for the branch tip, and every live caller moves to them. Filesystem readers (read_records, walltime, site generator, backtest, decisions.rs) take their root from ensure_records_worktree, a detached worktree at the tip that is created or fast-forwarded on demand under a lock. Exact-tree Records::load and RecordSet::load stay for gate reconcile, history and attribution, and for historical-commit tests. Edits are allowed anywhere in the named crates (the request's Files line), not only in the expected-deliverables list. The seam table in docs/design/records-history.md (about lines 488-510) is the inventory. Equivalence and no-records tests live in the files they exercise, plus one new integration test file in athena-cli/tests.

decisions.choice: Use the branch only when its tip has at least one entry under records/. Otherwise use the given treeish or working tree.
decisions.reason: Keeps the existing fixtures (landings-only branch) unchanged and implements the pre-cutover fallback.

rejected.option: Use the branch whenever the ref exists
rejected.why: Readers go empty in landings-only fixtures.

rejected.option: Fail when the branch is absent

decisions.choice: The worktree is detached at the tip. Each call compares HEAD to the tip and updates under a lock file.
decisions.reason: Git refuses a second checkout of a branch, and a detached worktree never moves the ref, so it cannot act as a writer.

rejected.option: Worktree with the branch checked out
rejected.why: Git blocks it, and it risks looking like a writer.

decisions.choice: xtask already depends on athena-data and athena-git (checked in xtask/Cargo.toml). The walltime reader (xtask/src/walltime.rs:83, root.join("records/jobs")) and the site generator call records_worktree_path from athena-data. xtask needs no athena-core dependency, so it gets a small ensure function that runs git worktree add or checkout through athena-git. Alternatively, xtask takes the root from the athena CLI.
decisions.reason: Avoids a dependency cycle or a heavy dependency. The path is still defined once, in athena-data.

rejected.option: Add athena-core as an xtask dependency

decisions.choice: The criterion 3 scan test in xtask covers three things in non-test sources. First, any string literal starting with records/ or equal to "records", including records/jobs. Second, calls to Records::load( and RecordSet::load( . Third, read_records(self.git.dir()) style roots. Each has an allow-list: the helper, fallback, writers, gate reconcile/history/attribution, and store.rs internals.
decisions.reason: A join("records")-only scan misses records/jobs paths and git-tree readers.

rejected.why: It proves less than criterion 3 asks.

decisions.choice: Leave writers and admission.rs's records/ guard alone. Touch admission.rs and records_import.rs only to share constants.
decisions.reason: Out of scope: only readers move.

demonstrations.method: Tests build a scratch repo with a records/ fixture and run import_records at C0. For each named reader they compare the result with records/ in the tree against the result from the branch (the tree reader or the worktree root) after records/ is removed from the tree. The readers are Records::load_current, RecordSet::load_current, read_records, walltime, status, forecast, scoring, retry carry, auditor, introspection and the site generator. Each result must be non-empty.
demonstrations.observes: Equal, non-empty results from both sources for every reader.
demonstrations.fails_without: A reader still reading the working tree sees nothing once records/ is deleted, so its output is empty and differs.

demonstrations.method: A test runs the status and forecast handlers with output captured. It uses a scratch checkout with ATHENA_STATE_DIR set to a tempdir, after import and removal of records/ from the working tree. It compares the output with the run that had records/.
demonstrations.observes: Both succeed and the output matches the records/ run.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the redirect (status.rs and the forecast source), status and forecast see no records and error or differ.

demonstrations.method: An athena-data unit test asserts that records_worktree_path equals repo_state_dir(..).join(constant). The xtask scan test checks non-test sources for records/ literals, Records::load calls and RecordSet::load calls outside the allow-list.
demonstrations.observes: One definition, and no stray reader.
demonstrations.fails_without: A reader with a records/ literal or an exact-tree load outside the allow-list trips the scan.

demonstrations.method: Run the full suite with no records branch in the existing fixtures. Run cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check.
demonstrations.observes: All pre-existing tests pass unchanged, and clippy and fmt are clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the fallback, no-branch tests read nothing and fail.

open_questions: Does xtask's site generator read records through git trees or through the filesystem? If it uses trees, load_current is not available to it without athena-core, so it uses the filesystem worktree.
The seam table in docs/design/records-history.md lines ~488-510 should be checked against the grep inventory at implementation time. The grep shows 142 occurrences in 38 files, tests included.
Do any writers still write records/ on main after the cutover job? They are out of scope.
